rubrics.justification: The response appropriately identifies a very poor-quality blastocyst consistent with 1DD and reasonably comments on poorly defined ICM and sparse/irregular TE, but it overinterprets image details and contains some imprecision about stage/day context without discussing limits of image-based assessment.

It integrates age, ovarian reserve, prior IVF outcomes, endometrium, sperm parameters, and lifestyle with embryo quality well, though it somewhat overstates implications of prior losses and male factor in relation to this specific embryo.

The reasoning is generally logical and consistent: poor morphology drives prognosis despite favorable maternal factors. Minor issues include speculative links to aneuploidy and some overstatement around Day 4 developmental interpretation.

Most recommendations are broadly IVF-consistent, but suggesting thrombophilia screening and strongly recommending PGT-A in a 26-year-old based mainly on prior biochemical losses is not fully guideline-concordant; some statements about cancellation/selection are more opinion-based than guideline-based.

Provides clear counseling points, prognosis framing, transfer considerations, and future-cycle planning steps. It is useful clinically, though some recommendations are broader than necessary and not fully prioritized.
